preamble: Fronting and assibilation of the voiceless palatal stop [c] to the alveolar affricate [ts]. In Standard Modern Greek /k/ is realized as palatal [c] before front vowels. In most of the Cyclades and in the Old Athenian group (Aegina, Megara, old Athens) this palatal is fronted further to [ts] and merges with original /ts/. Greek linguists call this tsitakism, e.g. Κυριακή /kiriaˈki/ 'Sunday' > [tsirjaˈtsi]. Newton (1972) derives the [ts] through an earlier [tʃ] stage, and Megara has both [tʃ] and [ts] outcomes.

languageExamples.language: Modern Greek (Cycladic and Old Athenian dialects)

examples.note: Tsitakism: the palatal allophone [c] of /k/ before front vowels is fronted to [ts] and merges with original /ts/; the feature was also shared by Old Athenian.
Tsitakism in the Megara dialect (Old Athenian group); the change of the first vowel is unrelated.
Megara also keeps the hiatus -έα where the standard language has synizesis -ιά.
